note: The train / held-out split for Phase 0, DECLARED UP FRONT rather than derived at run time. docs/lora-operator-guide.md §5: 'Eval set — held out, never trained on. A slice of repos reserved from the start, including the four hand-ground-truthed ones, so the pass-rate number means something.' Reserving the split in a committed file is what makes that checkable: lib/corpus.mjs refuses to build a dataset unless every manifest row appears exactly once across the two lists AND every row carrying a `groundTruth` path is on the held-out side. Move a row between lists deliberately, in a commit, or not at all — a split that drifts silently makes every pass-rate number downstream incomparable to the last one.

heldOutWhy.example-voting-app: Small compose stack — keeps a cheap, fast row in the eval set so the harness can be exercised without waiting on a large scan.
heldOutWhy.sock-shop: A microservice shape NOT represented by any ground-truthed row's topology, so the eval set is not four variations of one thing.
heldOutWhy.vite: A library/tooling repo rather than a service mesh — the eval must include a repo where 'add a cache in front of X' is an awkward ask, because users will ask it there anyway.
heldOutWhy.django: Large framework monolith. The hardest digest shape we have; if the tuned model only holds format on tidy microservice repos we need that to show up in the number, not hide.
